en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eighteenth Chapter
The Discussion on the Transition between Jhānas: Does one transition from a jhāna to a jhāna?
Yes, [one does].
"One passes from the first jhāna to the third jhāna"?
One should not say so... [and so on] ... "One passes from one jhāna to another"? One should not say so.
“Yes,” you say.
“Does one pass from the second jhāna to the fourth jhāna?
You must not say so … [and so on] … .
Does one pass from the first jhāna to the second jhāna? Yes.

Is that which is the turning toward, the inclination, and the aspiration for the arising of the first jhāna, the very same turning toward, inclination, and aspiration for the arising of the second jhāna? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … When one passes from the first jhāna to the second jhāna, should it not be said:

“That which was the turning toward, … [and so on] … the aspiration for the arising of the first jhāna, that same is the turning toward, … [and so on] … the aspiration for the arising of the second jhāna”?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does the second jhāna arise for one who does not turn back [toward lower states] …pe… for one who does not direct [the mind]?
You should not say so …pe…
Is it not the case that the second jhāna arises for one who turns toward it … pe … and arises for one who directs his intention toward it? Yes.
If the second jhāna arises for one who turns toward it … pe … and arises for one who directs his intention toward it, then indeed, sir, you should not say [that it does not arise].
“One passes from the first jhāna to the second jhāna,” ...
[and so on] ... One passes from the first jhāna to the second jhāna? Yes.
Is the first jhāna produced by one who attends to the danger in sensual pleasures?
Yes. Is the second jhāna produced by one who attends to the danger in sensual pleasures? Yes.
It should not be said so… [as before]… Is the first jhāna with applied thought (vitakka) and sustained thought (vicāra)? Yes.
Is the second jhāna with applied thought and sustained thought?
One should not say so... [etc.
...Does one pass from the first jhāna to the second jhāna?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is that very first jhāna the same as the second jhāna?
You should not say so… [and so on]…
Does one pass from the second jhāna to the third jhāna?

Yes. Is that which is the turning toward, the inclination, and the aspiration for the arising of the second jhāna, the very same as the turning toward, the inclination, and the aspiration for the arising of the third jhāna? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … When one passes from the second jhāna to the third jhāna, should it not be said:

“That which was the turning toward, … [and so on] … the aspiration for the arising of the second jhāna, that same is the turning toward, … [and so on] … the aspiration for the arising of the third jhāna”?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Does the third jhāna arise for one who does not turn back [from it] …pe… for one who does not direct [the mind] toward it?
[The respondent replies: “One should certainly not say so …pe…”
But is it not the case that the third jhāna arises for one who turns toward it …pe… and arises for one who directs his intention toward it?
Yes, it is so.
If the third jhāna arises for one who turns toward it …pe… and arises for one who directs his intention toward it, then indeed, sir, you should not say [that it does not arise].
“One passes from the second jhāna to the third jhāna.
Does one pass from the second jhāna to the third jhāna? Yes.
Is the second jhāna produced by attending to the danger in applied and sustained thought?
Yes. Is the third jhāna produced by attending to the danger in applied and sustained thought? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the second jhāna accompanied by rapture? Yes.
Is the third jhāna accompanied by rapture?
One should not say so …pe… Does one pass from the second jhāna to the third jhāna?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is that very second jhāna the third jhāna?
One should not speak thus … [and so on] … No.
Does one transition from the third jhāna to the fourth jhāna? Yes.

Is that which is the turning toward, the inclination, and the aspiration for the arising of the third jhāna, the very same as the turning toward, the inclination, and the aspiration for the arising of the fourth jhāna?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … One passes from the third jhāna to the fourth jhāna; should it not be said that “the turning toward,
… [as before] … the aspiration for the arising of the third jhāna is itself the turning toward, … [as before] … the aspiration for the arising of the fourth jhāna”?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does the fourth jhāna arise for one who does not turn back [from it] …pe… does it arise for one who does not direct [the mind] toward it?
You should not say so …pe…
But is it not the case that the fourth jhāna arises for one who turns toward it …pe… and arises for one who directs his intention toward it?
Yes, it is so.
If the fourth jhāna arises for one who turns toward it …pe… and arises for one who directs his intention toward it, then indeed, you should not say [that it does not arise].
“One passes from the third jhāna to the fourth jhāna.
Does one pass from the third jhāna to the fourth jhāna? Yes.
Is the third jhāna produced by one who attends to rapture as a disadvantage? Yes.
Is the fourth jhāna produced by one who attends to rapture as a disadvantage?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is the third jhāna accompanied by pleasure? Yes.
Is the fourth jhāna accompanied by pleasure?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...Does one pass from the third jhāna to the fourth jhāna?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is that very third jhāna the fourth jhāna?
“One should not speak thus” … [and so on] … “No.”
Is it not to be said that one passes from one jhāna to another jhāna?
Yes, it is.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
"Here, monks, a monk, quite secluded from sensual pleasures...
enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna"?
Is that indeed the Sutta? Yes.
Therefore, one passes from one jhāna to another.
The Discussion on the Transition of Jhāna is finished.
